title: Pizza Bianca
subtitle: Roman-style white pizza with olive oil and rosemary
excerpt: Pizza bianca is a Roman flatbread made with olive oil, coarse sea salt, and rosemary. There is no tomato and no cheese. It is eaten as a snack, with mortadella stuffed inside, or alongside cured meats and olives. The texture is chewy in the centre and crisp underneath.
sourceNotes: Pizza bianca is the bread of Rome, sold by weight from bakeries and eaten throughout the day. The Roman version is distinct from the Ligurian focaccia and the Neapolitan pizza bianca: it is thinner and less oily than focaccia, with a chewy crumb and a deeply flavoured crust. The bakery Forno Campo de' Fiori in Rome is among the most cited references for the traditional style.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 large flatbread, about 30 x 40 cm, serving 4 as a side
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough rests overnight, so start the night before. The bianca is best eaten the day it is baked.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional. Preheat with a heavy baking tray inside.

content.text: Pizza bianca is the white bread of Rome: no tomato, no cheese, just dough, olive oil, salt, and rosemary. It is closer to a thin focaccia than a pizza. Bakeries in Rome sell it warm from the oven by the slice, sometimes stuffed with mortadella. At home it works as a side bread, a snack, or the base for a simple cold lunch with cured meats.
The dough rests overnight so it develops flavour. Make it the night before, then shape and bake it the next day in 30 minutes.

items.prepNote: about a quarter of a 7 g sachet

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and 2 tablespoons of the olive oil. Mix until a rough dough forms, then knead briefly for 3 to 4 minutes. It will be soft and slightly sticky.
Cover the bowl and leave at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate overnight.

Take the dough out of the fridge 1 hour before baking. Oil a large baking tray generously. Tip the dough onto the tray and use your fingers to press and stretch it gently to fill the tray. If it springs back, leave it for 10 minutes and try again.

Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil over the top. Scatter the rosemary leaves and press them gently into the dough. Sprinkle with sea salt flakes. Leave to rest for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 230°C.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until the top is golden and the base is crisp when you lift an edge with a palette knife. Cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes before cutting.

Pizza bianca is Roman street food. It is sold warm by the slice from wood-fired bakeries all over the city, and the version stuffed with mortadella is a Roman classic. The bakeries are open from very early in the morning, and the bianca that comes out of the oven at 6 am and sold in paper bags is eaten on the way to work.
